correctness.rationale: For X=(0^a1^b)^omega, p=a+b, and k=mp+r, the zero count of consecutive blocks equals ma+g_j(u) with g_j obtained as differences of the exact run-prefix function F. Every g_j is affine between the <=2(q+1)+2 residues -jr and a-jr (j=0..q); for each interval, equality of any two integer-affine functions is either identically true, impossible, or one integer root. Removing the union of O(q^2) roots across O(q) intervals exactly counts successful q-antipower phases in O(q^3 log q) arithmetic independent of p,k. Three distinct counts require at least {0,1,2}; for s=min(a,b)=1 none exist, while s=2 requires 3k>p, except the exhaustive p=4 and p=6 cases. For s=2,t=3 or t>=5, k=floor(p/3)+1 attains the bound at exactly 2 phases. For s>=3, the six realizable length-six transition factors show K=2 and count 2+2[a=3]+2[b=3]. Independent direct cyclic-phase brute force for all 225 ordered 1<=a,b<=15 verified the onset and exact first-length multiplicities, including all impossible residues. The infinite bounds rest on the floor-prefix derivation, not the finite experiments.
